finding.description: The classification of a failing problem's refutation: a genuine defect of the code under test (`error`, on a problem that is not deprecated), a wrong statement (`spec_bug`, on a deprecated one), a gap of the machine model (`model_gap`, with a `pointer` to the missing instruction or feature) or `unclear`

pointer.description: What it points at: the missing instruction or feature (required for `model_gap`), a bug report, a commit

affected_versions.description: `error` only: the versions the defect affects

expected_open.description: An open problem expected to stay open for a metatheoretic reason about the ambient theory (Lean's type theory with the axioms its proofs may use), not about an object theory the statement talks about: Con(ZFC) is not an example. Never for an ordinary unproved problem. Its judgement's `expect`, if any, is `OPN`

reason.description: `independent` (known to be neither provable nor refutable in the ambient theory) or `consistency` (implies the consistency of the ambient theory itself, so Gödel's second incompleteness theorem applies to that theory)

note.description: Why the reason holds of the ambient theory (Lean's), not only of an object theory

pointer.description: A citation or URL for the metatheoretic result
